stages.name: Mid-season (FAO-56: full cover to start of maturity; covers flowering and most grain/pod filling)

sources: Frontiers in Genetics (2023) 14:1206451: temperatures above 40 C cause terminal heat stress at the reproductive stage, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2023.1206451/full
Scientia Horticulturae (2016): >40/28 C at the reproductive stage highly detrimental to flower production and pod set, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304423816305350

Physiology of Plants / Russ. J. Plant Physiol. (2024): grows most efficiently at 27-35 C; thermotolerant in vegetative phase, sensitive in reproductive phase, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134/S1021443724605421
thresholds.notes: Critical 40 C at the reproductive stage is stated by two peer-reviewed studies. Warning 35 C is the top of the 27-35 C efficient-growth range, read as daily maximum.

notes: Legume: may serve as a soil-health indicator, which does not by itself prove improved soil health.
evidence_gaps: Heat limit applies to the mid-season (flowering and pod filling) only; sources describe mung bean as heat-tolerant in the vegetative phase.
Waterlogging and disease thresholds are not yet sourced; drought uses the FAO-56 water balance. Sources note sensitivity to waterlogging and seed spoilage from high moisture at maturity.
Stage lengths are FAO-56 Table 11 general values, scaled to each season; FAO says they 'may vary substantially' by region and variety and local data should be preferred.
